system.name: sysspec-demo
system.title: sysspec demo
system.summary: A small commerce system specified end to end: orders accepted over HTTP, order lifecycle and payment settlement carried as events, and the historical record of both published as data contracts. Every toolkit change must keep it green, so what you read here is what the gates actually enforce.

services.name: orders

services.summary: Owns the Order aggregate. Accepts order placement over HTTP, emits lifecycle events, and consumes payment settlement to close orders out.

artifacts.summary: Events emitted and consumed by the Order aggregate.
Synchronous order placement and lookup API.
Acceptance criteria for order placement and guaranteed event publication.
artifacts.text:
Feature: Placing an order
  As a customer
  I want to place an order
  So that it is fulfilled once payment settles

  These scenarios are acceptance criteria, not suggestions. An
  implementation that fails any of them is wrong. If a scenario is
  itself wrong, that is a versioned change to this file.

  Background:
    Given the customer "c-1001" exists

  Scenario: A valid order is accepted and its event is guaranteed
    When the customer places an order for 2 units of "SKU-RED" at 1250 pence
    Then the response status is 201
    And the order status is "placed"
    And the order total is 2500 pence
    And an "OrderPlaced" event is guaranteed to be published for the order

  Scenario: The order and its event succeed or fail together
    Given event publication is unavailable
    When the customer places an order for 1 unit of "SKU-RED" at 1250 pence
    Then the response status is 201
    And the "OrderPlaced" event is published once publication recovers
    And no order ever exists without its "OrderPlaced" event

  Scenario: Replaying an idempotency key returns the original order
    Given the customer placed an order with "Idempotency-Key" header "idem-99"
    When the same request is retried with "Idempotency-Key" header "idem-99"
    Then the response status is 201
    And the same order_id is returned
    And no second "OrderPlaced" event is published

  Scenario: A conflicting body on a used idempotency key is rejected
    Given the customer placed an order with "Idempotency-Key" header "idem-99"
    When a different order body is sent with "Idempotency-Key" header "idem-99"
    Then the response status is 409
    And the problem body carries an error_code and message

  Scenario: Order events are CloudEvents envelopes
    When the customer places an order for 2 units of "SKU-RED" at 1250 pence
    Then an "OrderPlaced" event is published on "orders.placed.v2"
    And the envelope carries specversion "1.0", a unique id and a time
    And the envelope source is /orders and its type is com.hungovercoders.orders.placed.v2
    And the envelope subject is the order_id, with datacontenttype "application/json"
    And the data carries the order_id, customer_id, placed_at and total_pence
    And handlers dedupe on the envelope id, not the natural key

  Scenario: Cancellation is a CloudEvents envelope too
    Given the customer placed an order
    When the order is cancelled because "out_of_stock"
    Then an "OrderCancelled" event is published on "orders.cancelled.v2"
    And its data carries the order_id, cancelled_at and reason

  Scenario Outline: An order is only cancelled for a declared reason
    Given the customer placed an order
    When the order is cancelled because "<reason>"
    Then the cancellation is accepted and records that reason
    And a reason outside this list is rejected

    Examples:
      | reason           | meaning                                          |
      | customer_request | the customer asked for the order to be cancelled |
      | payment_failed   | no payment settled inside the window             |
      | out_of_stock     | the order cannot be fulfilled from stock         |

  Scenario: A settled payment marks the order paid
    Given the customer placed an order
    When a "PaymentSettled" event arrives on "payments.settled.v2" for that order_id
    Then the order status is "paid"
    And replaying the same envelope id does not change the order again

  Scenario: An order can be fetched by its id
    Given the customer placed an order via placeOrder
    When the order is fetched by order_id via getOrder
    Then the response status is 200
    And the order carries the order_id, customer_id, status and total_pence

  Scenario: Fetching an unknown order returns 404
    When an unknown order_id is fetched via getOrder
    Then the response status is 404
    And the problem body carries an error_code and message

  Scenario Outline: Orders must have at least one valid line
    When the customer places an order with <lines>
    Then the response status is 400
    And the problem body carries an error_code and message

    Examples:
      | lines                       |
      | no lines                    |
      | a line quantity of 0        |
      | a negative unit_price_pence |
      | a line missing its sku      |

artifacts.summary: Append-only historical record of the order lifecycle events.

description.purpose: Append-only historical record of the Order aggregate's events. One row per event, mirroring the AsyncAPI payloads on orders.placed.v2 and orders.cancelled.v2 field for field - the stream is ephemeral, this table is the record.
description.usage: Order lifecycle analytics, audit, and replay/backfill for downstream consumers that joined after the fact. Not a source for current order state - use the orders service API for that.
description.limitations: Delivery upstream is at-least-once; rows are deduplicated on the CloudEvents envelope id, so exactly one row per event. Events land within minutes but ordering across event types is only guaranteed per order_id.

context.instructions: This is the event history of the Order aggregate, one row per event, never updated in place. Count orders from order_placed_events and treat order_cancelled_events as a separate fact joined on order_id; an order can appear in both. Money is always integer pence in total_pence - never divide before aggregating.

verifiedStatements.question: How many orders were placed on a given day?
verifiedStatements.answer: Count rows in order_placed_events where placed_at falls in the day, in the placed_at timezone. The table is deduplicated on event_id, so no DISTINCT is needed.

verifiedStatements.question: What proportion of orders are cancelled, and why?
verifiedStatements.answer: Join order_cancelled_events to order_placed_events on order_id and group by reason. reason is a closed vocabulary of three values.

verifiedStatements.question: What is the value of an order?
verifiedStatements.answer: total_pence, an integer number of pence covering the whole order. There is no per-line breakdown in this record.

constraints.constraint: Never present this as current order state. An order cancelled after the last event you read still reads as placed here; the orders service API is the source for current state.
Never treat a missing order_cancelled_events row as proof an order was fulfilled - it only means no cancellation event has landed.

services.name: payments
services.title: Payments
services.summary: Authorises and settles payments against orders. Publishes settlement events and a daily reconciliation dataset.

artifacts.summary: Daily settled-payments table for finance reconciliation.

description.purpose: Daily reconciliation of settled payments for finance. One row per settled payment, partitioned by settlement date.
description.usage: Finance close and chargeback investigation. Not a source for real-time balances — use the payments service API for that.
description.limitations: Settlement date is the processor's, not ours, so late arrivals can backfill up to 3 days. Do not treat a partition as final until D+3.

context.instructions: This is the finance-facing reconciliation of settled payments, derived from the payment event history. One row per settled payment. Money is integer pence; sum amount_pence rather than averaging rates.

verifiedStatements.question: What settled yesterday?
verifiedStatements.answer: The rows in yesterday's settled_at partition - but that partition is not final until D+3, so a figure quoted before then can move.

verifiedStatements.question: How does this differ from the payment event history?
verifiedStatements.answer: Same settlements, shaped for finance close: one row per payment with no CloudEvents envelope columns. The event history is the record it derives from.

constraints.constraint: Never report a settlement-date partition as final before D+3 - late arrivals from the processor still backfill it.
Never use this for real-time balances; it is a daily product.

schema.name: settled_payments
schema.description: One row per settled payment, partitioned by settlement date.

context.instructions: Partitioned by settled_at. Treat the most recent three days as provisional: the processor backfills late arrivals up to D+3.

properties.name: settled_at
properties.description: Processor settlement time - the partition key; late arrivals backfill up to D+3.

quality.query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments_daily_settled WHERE amount_pence < 0

description.purpose: Append-only historical record of payment settlement events. One row per event, mirroring the AsyncAPI payload on payments.settled.v2 field for field - the stream is ephemeral, this table is the record.
description.usage: Settlement analytics, audit, and replay/backfill for downstream consumers that joined after the fact. The daily reconciliation product (payments-daily) is derived from this record.
description.limitations: Delivery upstream is at-least-once; rows are deduplicated on the CloudEvents envelope id, so exactly one row per settlement (settlement is terminal). Not a source for real-time balances - use the payments service API for that.

context.instructions: This is the settlement event history, one row per settled payment, never updated in place. Settlement is terminal: a payment settles once or not at all, so there is no later row to supersede one. Money is always integer pence in amount_pence. Join to the order record on order_id when a question spans both.

verifiedStatements.question: How much settled on a given day?
verifiedStatements.answer: Sum amount_pence over rows whose settled_at falls in the day. That is processor settlement time, not order time.

verifiedStatements.question: Which orders have been paid?
verifiedStatements.answer: The distinct order_id values present here. An order with no row has not settled - it may still be in flight.

verifiedStatements.question: Can one order settle more than once?
verifiedStatements.answer: No. payment_id is unique and settlement is terminal, so at most one settlement row exists per payment.

constraints.constraint: Never use this as a real-time balance or a payment status check - it is an event record with minutes of lag; the payments service API answers those.

artifacts.summary: Acceptance criteria for settlement and reversal handling.
artifacts.text:
Feature: Settling a payment
  Settlement is terminal. Authorisation is not.

  Scenario: Settlement emits exactly one event
    Given an authorised payment "p-1" for order "o-1" of 2500 pence
    When the processor confirms settlement
    Then a "PaymentSettled" event is published on "payments.settled.v2"
    And the event data amount_pence is 2500

  Scenario: Settlement events are CloudEvents envelopes
    Given an authorised payment "p-3" for order "o-3" of 1000 pence
    When the processor confirms settlement
    Then a "PaymentSettled" event is published on "payments.settled.v2"
    And the envelope carries specversion "1.0", a unique id and a time
    And the envelope source is /payments and its type is com.hungovercoders.payments.settled.v2
    And the envelope subject is the payment_id, with datacontenttype "application/json"
    And the data carries the payment_id, order_id, settled_at and amount_pence
    And handlers dedupe on the envelope id

  Scenario: Settlement is anchored to an observed order placement
    Given an "OrderPlaced" event arrived on "orders.placed.v2" for order "o-4"
    When the payment for "o-4" is authorised and the processor confirms settlement
    Then the "PaymentSettled" event's order_id matches the placed order

  Scenario: Duplicate settlement callbacks are idempotent
    Given payment "p-1" has already settled
    When the processor sends the settlement callback again
    Then no second "PaymentSettled" event is published

  Scenario: A reversal after authorisation does not emit settlement
    Given an authorised payment "p-2"
    When the authorisation is reversed
    Then no "PaymentSettled" event is published for "p-2"

the envelope source is /payments and its type is com.hungovercoders.payments.settled.v2
the envelope subject is the payment_id, with datacontenttype "application/json"
the data carries the payment_id, order_id, settled_at and amount_pence
handlers dedupe on the envelope id

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant svc as Payments
    participant c_payments_settled_v2 as payments.settled.v2
    Note over svc: When the processor confirms settlement
    svc-)c_payments_settled_v2: PaymentSettled

scenarios.title: Settlement is anchored to an observed order placement

steps.text: an "OrderPlaced" event arrived on "orders.placed.v2" for order "o-4"
the payment for "o-4" is authorised and the processor confirms settlement
the "PaymentSettled" event's order_id matches the placed order

scenarios.sequence_mermaid:

    participant svc as Payments
    participant c_payments_settled_v2 as payments.settled.v2
    c_orders_placed_v2--)svc: OrderPlaced
    svc-)c_payments_settled_v2: PaymentSettled

scenarios.title: Duplicate settlement callbacks are idempotent

steps.text: payment "p-1" has already settled
the processor sends the settlement callback again
no second "PaymentSettled" event is published

scenarios.sequence_mermaid:

scenarios.title: A reversal after authorisation does not emit settlement

steps.text: an authorised payment "p-2"
the authorisation is reversed
no "PaymentSettled" event is published for "p-2"
